acts.desc: Host Ira Glass remembers one of his favorite jobs, as a temp typist working at night in New York City. And we hear from a group of teenagers who create unique fun during the middle of the night when none of their classmates are awake.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Adam Davidson and Chana Joffe-Walt from Planet Money head to the Hunts Point Market in the Bronx, a bustling area of vegetable and fruit commerce that only comes alive at night. Planet Money is a co-production of NPR News and This American Life.
acts.credits: By Adam Davidson, Chana Joffe-Walt, Planet Money
acts.title: Orange You Glad I Didn’t Say Banana?

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Jenifer Hixson tells the story of walking alone at night, and meeting a woman who was out for the very same reason. Jenifer performed the story live in front of an audience at the storytelling series The Moth.
acts.title: It Was A Dark And Smoky Night

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: When a new Chick-Fil-A sandwich shop opens, people line up 24 hours in advance to be one of the hundred people to get a free year's worth of chicken sandwiches. Comedian/musician Dave Hill and writer Shaina Feinberg headed down to Orlando, Florida to experience the night before an opening.
acts.title: The Early Bird Catches The Chicken

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Producer Nancy Updike speaks with Specialist Lindsay Freeland of the Oregon National Guard about the trips Freeland takes at night in Iraq, providing security for convoys heading to forward operating bases.
acts.title: Midnight Run

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: Producer Jane Feltes talks with her parents about staying up at night with a sick child—specifically, after Jane had a serious injury when she was six.
acts.title: Bump In The Night
